biography.plain_text: Gerald Francis Bean was an American car dealer who founded Kendall Toyota in Miami in 1969 and developed it into a family-owned automotive group. His dealerships represented Toyota and Lexus across South Florida, creating the business that became Bean Automotive Group. After his death, daughter Lori Bean became its owner and dealer principal.

long_biography.plain_text:
Selling Kendall Toyota did not end Gerald Bean's involvement with the Miami dealership he had built. He repurchased the business two years later in 1999, restoring direct control of an operation that had become one of the country's largest Toyota outlets.

Bean had already gained national recognition for fleet sales during the dealership's first decade. He later expanded through Toyota and Lexus franchises, creating a group of South Florida dealerships rather than a single showroom. Florida filings also placed him in management roles across related dealership and investment entities, reflecting the wider business structure behind the retail sites.
